messages:
alex: heads-up — saw a p95 regression on mixtral-canary around 10:22 UTC, small but consistent after last kernel heuristics change. p50 fine, p95 +18% on generation-heavy traces

marta: linking the trace dump? can you paste the query that reproduces?

alex: pasted a short repro below. note it hits byte-fallback on tokenizer for some user prompts (weird chat templates):

```
input = "User: \"Attached file: (binary)\"\nAssistant:"
model: mixtral-8x
seq_len: 1024
observed: selected_kernel: byte_fallback, kv_cache_miss_ratio: 0.42, gen_latency_ms: 120 -> 140
```

alex: profiler snapshot: kernel_picker chose byte path at step 1 because tokenized.byte_fallback=true, but later tokens would have fit normal path. leads to 1.8x per-token overhead on the first chunk

perf-bot: p50: 78ms -> 81ms (+3.8%), p95: 210ms -> 248ms (+18.1%), tokens/s: 310 -> 254 (-18%) for canary bucket

marta: ok. initial theory: tokenizer emitted an unexpected special token sequence (BOS/EOS + escaped binary markers) that bumped token count and triggered fallback. also see RoPE scaling change in the config that changed kernel-selection thresholds (we recently tightened kernel_thresholds.max_seq to 512)

jin: curious — is kv-cache thrashing playing a role? if prefix lengths vary a lot across batched requests, we can lose cache locality and KV memory access pattern degenerates. could explain p95 tail

alex: yes — traces show alternating short/long prefixes in the same batch. batcher.policy=latency currently groups up to 8 requests irrespective of prefix length, so we end up with mixed cache hotness

marta: proposed fixes (quick canary):
- bump kernel_selection.v2.min_confidence so we prefer float8-optimized kernel for mixtral when heads==kv_heads
- change batcher.grouping to `prefer_same_prefix_len=true` (soft constraint)
- patch tokenizer to collapse the escaped-binary marker into a single safe token (avoid byte-fallback)

jin: +1 for batching change. cheap and should improve KV hits. tokenizer patch needs QA but can be toggled behind a flag

alex: i'll prepare a small canary with 5% traffic and explicit fallback policy: fallback->use-mixtral-quant in 200ms, and metrics hook to abort if p95 reg > 10%

deploy-bot: deploy request created: canary/mixtral-kv-batching-1803501234 (5% traffic) — started at 1803501250

perf-bot: initial canary measurements (first 5m): p95 down to 226ms (from 248), tokens/s 276. still worse than baseline but improving. Croned full-profile run scheduled

marta: also adding a targeted kernel-picker log to emit `reason=tokenizer_fallback` so we can correlate next time. tiny change, low risk

alex: action items:
- marta to land kernel_selection tweak + logging flag (PR in review)
- jin to update batcher to prefer_same_prefix_len (feature flag)
- alex to add canary guard and run tokenizer QA on escaped-binary case

jin: will also run ablation comparing keeping kernel_thresholds.max_seq=512 vs 768 for mixtral on same HW (NVIDIA A100-sim). might be that RoPE scaling change costs us when sequence distribution skews

alex: thanks. if canary looks stable after 30m we'll roll to 50% and then to general. if p95 crosses +10% rollback immediately. :thumbsup:

marta: noted — leaving perf hooks in place. will follow up with a short perf summary once kernel logs accumulate

alex: thanks everyone. saved the trace to s3://redwood-dev/traces/1803501234/mixtral_canary_raw.json for deeper offline profiling
